chats.answer:
Yes, laptop screen extenders work with the MacBook Air M3 (2024), including portable dual-screen extenders that attach to the sides of your laptop.

However, there's an important limitation: the M3 MacBook Air supports a maximum of two external displays natively, and only when the laptop lid is closed.

What works with your M3 MacBook Air?

Setup

	

Compatible?




Built-in screen + 1 external screen

	

 Yes




Built-in screen + 2 external screens

	

 With DisplayLink




Closed MacBook + 2 external screens

	

 Yes, natively




Built-in screen + 3 external screens

	

 With suitable DisplayLink hardware

The key is DisplayLink

If you're buying a laptop screen extender with two screens that unfold from the sides, you'll likely want one that supports DisplayLink technology.

DisplayLink lets your MacBook M3 run multiple independent external displays while keeping the built-in screen active.

Be aware that DisplayLink typically requires installing DisplayLink Manager and granting macOS screen-recording permission. It's excellent for productivity, but less ideal for gaming or high-refresh-rate video.

Apple confirms the native display limitation in its M3 external display support guide. DisplayLink's setup guide explains the additional software requirements.

One question before you buy

Are you looking for a dual-screen laptop extender like this?

Or just one additional portable screen?

The distinction matters because I can help you choose a model that actually supports three independent screens on your M3 MacBook Air, rather than one that only mirrors the display.

chats.answer:
Yes, laptop screen extenders work with the MacBook Air M3, including portable dual-screen extenders that attach to the sides of your laptop.

However, there's an important limitation: not all screen extenders are compatible with the M3 MacBook Air, especially models that add two external screens.

What the MacBook Air M3 supports

Configuration

	

Supported?




Built-in screen + 1 external screen

	

 Yes




Built-in screen + 2 external screens

	

 Not natively




Laptop closed + 2 external screens

	

 Yes




Built-in screen + 2 external screens using DisplayLink

	

 Yes, with compatible hardware and software

This matters because most dual-screen laptop extenders are designed to give you three screens total: your MacBook screen plus two additional displays.

Apple confirms these limitations in its official M3 display support guide.

What to look for when buying

Dual-screen extender (three screens total)

Choose one that explicitly supports M3 MacBooks using DisplayLink or another compatible USB graphics solution. Ordinary USB-C video output alone isn't enough for both extra screens.

Single-screen extender (two screens total)

Usually the easiest option. A compatible USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode extender should work without additional display drivers.

One question: Are you looking for an extender with one extra screen or two extra screens attached to your MacBook Air M3?

That determines which models will actually work.
